docs.title: About Unimined
docs.text: Welcome to Unimined, a unified Minecraft modding environment that supports both modern and legacy environments. Whether you're working with the latest Minecraft versions or exploring older builds, Unimined provides a comprehensive set of tools to help you build mods with ease.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Unified Modding Environment: Supports various Minecraft mod loaders and offers tools for a seamless experience across different modding platforms.
  • Custom Loader Support: Create and integrate your own loaders with the flexibility of Unimined.

  • just plain jarmodding

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Run configs authenticate through gradle properties/env vars — put them in the global gradle.properties so they never land in the repo:

unimined.auth.username=you@example.com
unimined.auth.password=...

The run configs pick them up — runs { } is top-level in 2.0:

runs {
    create("client") { /* auth flows from the properties above */ }
}

docs.title: Mappings
docs.text: Mappings provide the ability to remap minecraft into names you can actually use at runtime. As well as remapping to the production mappings that each modloader uses.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Mappings are used in the mappings block of the unimined.minecraft block in your build.gradle file.

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        mojmap()
    }
    ...
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        mojmap()
    }
    ...
}

some require a version number, or version string to be passed in as a parameter.

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        yarn 1
    }
    ...
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        yarn(1)
    }
    ...
}

docs.title: Overriding mappings
docs.text:
it is sometimes useful to override specific mappings, such as when using forge with yarn mappings, or when a mod is using yarn at dev, but you're using mojmap and it causes an issue.

unimined provides a DSL for inserting said mapping stubs, it's syntax is similar to umf's format.

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
...
    mappings {
        ...
        stubs(["source", "target1", "target2"]) {
            c(["sourceName", "target1Name", "target2Name"]) {// can change the target names of a class, or use null/empty list to skip
                m(["sourceMethodName;(LsourceType;)LreturnType;", "target1MethodName"]) // can change the target names of a method, or use nulls/empty list to skip
            }
        }
    }
...
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        ...
        stubs("source", "target1", "target2") {
            c("sourceName", "target1Name", "target2Name") { // can change the target names of a class, or use null/empty list to skip
                m("sourceMethodName;(LsourceType;)LreturnType;", "target1MethodName") // can change the target names of a method, or use nulls/empty list to skip
            }
        }
    }
    ...
}

real example, (1.20.6, neoforge fix for yarn):

GroovyKotlin 
stubs(["intermediary", "yarn"]) {
    c(["net/minecraft/class_1496"]) {
        m(["method_56680;()Lnet/minecraft/class_1263;", "getInventoryVanilla"])
    }
    c(["net/minecraft/class_329"]) {
        m(["method_1759;(Lnet/minecraft/class_332;F)V", "renderHotbarVanilla"])
    }
}

stubs("intermediary", "yarn") {
    c("net/minecraft/class_1496") {
        m("method_56680;()Lnet/minecraft/class_1263;", "getInventoryVanilla")
    }
    c("net/minecraft/class_329") {
        m("method_1759;(Lnet/minecraft/class_332;F)V", "renderHotbarVanilla")
    }
}

docs.title: Custom mapping sources
docs.text:
you can add a custom mapping source with the mapping function inside the mappings block.

for example. to add yarn this way (for some reason) you would do:

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        ...
        mapping("net.fabricmc:yarn:1.17.1+build.1:v2", "yarn") {
            requires "intermediary" // sets the source namespace to intermediary
            mapNamespace("named", "yarn") // renames the output ns to "yarn"
            provides("yarn", true) // defines the output ns as yarn and is named

            renest() // causes classes that aren't named to be nested under their parent class's name,
            // ie, net.minecraft.class_1234$class_1235 -> net.minecraft.NamedNameFor1234$class_1235
        }
    }
    ...
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        ...
        mapping("net.fabricmc:yarn:1.17.1+build.1:v2", "yarn") {
            requires("intermediary") // sets the source namespace to intermediary
            mapNamespace("named" to "yarn") // renames the output ns to "yarn"
            provides("yarn" to true) // defines the output ns as yarn and is named

            renest() // causes classes that aren't named to be nested under their parent class's name,
            // ie, net.minecraft.class_1234$class_1235 -> net.minecraft.NamedNameFor1234$class_1235
        }
    }
}

docs.title: DevNamespace
docs.text:
you can define which named mappings to use in dev with the devNamespace field in the mappings block. this also allows you to set the fallback namespace for if things aren't named in the dev namespace.

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        ...
        devNamespace "mojmap" // sets the dev namespace to mojmap
    }
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        ...
        devNamespace("mojmap") // sets the dev namespace to mojmap
    }
}

docs.title: Migrating from 1.x to 2.0
docs.text: Unimined 2.0 splits the monolithic unimined { } extension into per-domain plugins with their own extensions. Groovy scripts that call removed 1.x verbs now get a migration note naming the new form; Kotlin DSL scripts fail at compile time — this table maps old calls to their 2.0 equivalents.

docs.title: Environment configuration
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 unimined.minecraft(sourceSet) { } unimined.minecraft { } + per-source-set env (minecraft { sourceSet("main") { } }) unimined.reIndev(sourceSet) { } env-level infra config inside unimined.minecraft { } unimined.bta(sourceSet) { } same — env-level inside unimined.minecraft { }

Loader declaration moves onto the environment: loader("fabric", "0.16.0") / loader("fg1", "0.1.5") / env.jarmod("x") / env.fg1("x") / env.customSearge().

docs.title: Remap pipeline
docs.text: 1.x 2.0 remap hooks inside unimined { } unimined.remap { } — step verbs (unpick(...), applyClassTweaker {}, sourceRemap {}) per surface, both Groovy and Kotlin. Source remapping runs through UML's source remapper by default; jst {} remains as an explicit engine opt-in (verification/alternate engine), not a peer default unimined.migrateMappings(sourceSet) { } unimined.migrateMappings("main") { } (env id), or unimined.migrate { }

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text: The ~20 unimined.*Maven()/unimined.*Repos() helpers (fabricMaven, minecraftForgeMaven, curseMaven, jitpack, spigot, quiltMaven, ornitheMaven, legacyFabricMaven, neoForgedMaven, cleanroomRepos, modrinthMaven, …) are gone: loader repositories are auto-registered per environment in 2.0. Remove the calls; use a normal repositories {} block for anything custom. modsRemapRepo is likewise managed internally.

docs.title: Other moves
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 mod/transform config inside unimined { } unimined.mod { }, unimined.transform { } global toolchain toggle unimined.useToolchains = false env java override unimined.javaVersion (delegates to the main env)

Unknown or removed verbs raise a GradleException naming the replacement — read the message; it points here.

docs.title: Declared-source provider (legacydist)
docs.text:
New in 2.0: environments whose game jar has no manifest-backed provider declare the artifact directly instead of shipping a bespoke provider — BTA/ReIndev-style jars, pre-1.8 bukkit, offline/air-gapped artifacts:

unimined.minecraft.main.legacydist {
    file("libs/bta-7.3-client.jar")      // or maven("g:a:v"),
    // url("https://...", sha256 = "..."), producer("tool", "...")
    namespace = "official"               // jar's production namespace
    format = "obf"                       // optional — raw->dev remap view
}

legacydist {} selects provider("legacydist") implicitly; the jar is cached by content hash and reported with the declared namespace/format. URLs are pinned by SHA-256 (warned-but-allowed when omitted); maven coordinates resolve at declaration time.

docs.title: Modloaders
docs.text:
Unimined supports many modloaders — declared per-environment with loader("<name>", "<version>") inside a minecraft { } env:

unimined {
    minecraft {
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
        loader("forge", "47.2.0") // repeat = multiloader env
    }
}

Names come from the loader registry: fabric, quilt, forge, neoforge, cleanroom, flint, rift, foxloader, liteloader, craftbukkit, spigot, paper, plus era loaders like fg1 and pseudo-loaders jarmod, accessTransformer, accessWidener.

Non-native products nest their loader inside the product env — unimined { bta { loader("bta-babric", "…") } }, reindev { loader("foxloader", "…") }.

Loader "api" artifacts resolve via unimined.loaderApi(name, v) / loaderApiModule(name, module, v) — fabric-api, qsl, stationapi, osl — which also records the api modid into mod { depends }.

For the most up-to-date registry, see the loader spec source.

docs.title: Multiple Source Sets & Projects
docs.text:
2.0 rewrite. The 1.x unimined.minecraft(sourceSets.x) / combineWith(...) APIs are gone — see Migrating from 1.x.

Two shapes cover the 1.x use cases:

  • flat — several minecraft { } envs in one project, each bound to a source set;
  • multi-module — a common module + one subproject per loader (what unimined-cli new --modules generates).

docs.title: Flat: one env per source set
docs.text:
Each minecraft { sourceSet(...) { } } block is an independent environment — its own product, loader, mappings, runs. Envs with no sourceSet call bind to main.

unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("main")
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
    }

    minecraft {
        sourceSet("server")
        loader("forge", "47.2.0")
        side = Side.SERVER
    }
}

Run configurations come from each env's run { }; there is no combineWith — an env that should share another's classpath just points at the same source set or module dependency.

docs.title: Multi-module: common + per-loader subprojects
docs.text:
This is what unimined new mymod --modules --loader fabric=… --loader forge=… emits. Settings includes every module:

A loader module applies unimined, declares its env on main, and depends on :common for shared code:

common gets a loader-less env (MC classpath + mappings only); the loader jars land as modImplementation deps in each loader module.

docs.title: Planned template modes
docs.text:
unimined-cli generated examples feed unimined/Unimined-Templates (release → release/<mode>, snapshot → snapshot/<mode> branches, diff-gated).

mode 1.x branch status blocked by multiloader — (new) implemented — forge, fabric 1.x/forge-era implemented — jarmod modloadermp planned jarmod loader end-to-end bta special/bta implemented — reindev, nsss — implemented — expectplatform 1.21.4/fabric+neo-expectplatform planned ExpectPlatform 2.0 port forge-downgrading 1.7.10/forge-downgrading planned forge-downgrading spec

docs.title: Remapping
docs.text:
Mods you depend on are remapped onto your environment's mappings. Each minecraft { } env exposes mod* configurations scoped to its source set — modImplementation, modCompileOnly, modLocalRuntime:

dependencies {
    modImplementation("maven:coord")
    // loader api helpers resolve the coordinate for you:
    // modImplementation(unimined.loaderApi("fabric", "0.92.2+1.20.1"))
}

The remap pipeline itself is configured in unimined { remap { } } — step verbs like unpick(...), applyClassTweaker { }, and sourceRemap { } (UML source remapper by default; jst { } is the explicit opt-in).

docs.title: Run configurations
docs.text:
runs { } is a top-level block in 2.0 (it moved out of unimined { }). Each registered run gets a Gradle task + an IDE run config:

runs {
    create("client") {
        mainClass = "net.minecraft.client.main.Main"
        jvmArgs += "-Xmx2G"
        programArgs += "--accessToken=0"
    }
    create("server") {
        mainClass = "net.minecraft.server.Main"
    }
}

Envs produce run tasks automatically from their loader's defaults; create(name) { } adds custom ones. autoStop and other boot-time options live on the run config.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Add the following to the settings.gradle:

GroovyKotlin 
pluginManagement {
    repositories {
        maven {
            url = uri("https://maven.wagyourtail.xyz/releases")
        }
        maven {
            url = uri("https://maven.wagyourtail.xyz/snapshots")
        }
        mavenCentral() // highly recommended, but not required
        gradlePluginPortal {
            content {
                // this is not required either, unless jcenter goes down again, then it might fix things
                excludeGroup("org.apache.logging.log4j")
            }
        }
    }
}

pluginManagement {
    repositories {
        maven("https://maven.wagyourtail.xyz/releases")
        maven("https://maven.wagyourtail.xyz/snapshots")
        mavenCentral() // highly recommended, but not required
        gradlePluginPortal {
            content {
                // this is not required either, unless jcenter goes down again, then it might fix things
                excludeGroup("org.apache.logging.log4j")
            }
        }
    }
}

And the following to build.gradle:

GroovyKotlin 
plugins {
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined' version '1.4.1'
}

plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "1.4.1"
}

This will not actually add minecraft to your project as it must be configured.

docs.title: Adding Minecraft
docs.text:
to add minecraft to the main sourceSet, add the following (a full generated project looks like --8<-- snippets/flat-fabric.gradle.kts):

GroovyKotlin 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        version project.minecraftVersion
    side "combined" // default value

    mappings {
        mojmap()
    }

    fabric {
        loader project.fabricLoaderVersion
    }
}

val minecraftVersion: String by extra
val fabricLoaderVersion: String by extra

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version minecraftVersion
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
    side("combined") // default value

    mappings {
        mojmap()
    }

    fabric {
        loader(fabricLoaderVersion)
    }
}

for more details about what's available within the unimined.minecraft block, see The Api Source

docs.title: Standard Libraries
docs.text:
Loader "api" artifacts resolve through unimined.loaderApi(...) — the 2.0 port of 1.x's FabricLikeApiExtension (unimined.fabricApi, quiltFabric, station, osl, …):

dependencies {
    // whole api bundle → dependency coordinates
    modImplementation(unimined.loaderApi("fabric", "0.92.2+1.20.1"))
    // one sub-module
    modImplementation(unimined.loaderApiModule(
        "fabric", "fabric-api-base", "0.92.2+1.20.1"))
}

Registered providers: fabric, quilt, qsl, legacyfabric, stationapi/stationapi-snapshots, osl (Ornithe resolves per-MC-version modules via meta.ornithemc.net). Calling either helper also records the api's modid into mod { depends } automatically.
